structure: retinal photoreceptor types (rod and cone morphotypes)
measurement: count of photoreceptor types: one rod type and two cone types (one with a red oil droplet)
method: light and electron microscopy of fixed retina (ultrastructure)
conditions: Juvenile P. dolloi: eyes from three juveniles (TL 20.6, 20.2 and 24 cm) from the University of Bonn; the Table 2 footnote says all measurements are from one individual 20.6 cm TL. Light and electron microscopy of fixed retina (post-fixation shrinkage 6.3%). Authors also report one cone with yellow pigment of which 'there are only 36 cells of this type counted in the retina' (status uncertain), so the 'two cone types' count may be exceeded; eleven smaller red-droplet cones may be fixation-damaged red cones. Morphological types, not microspectrophotometry: spectral classes were not measured. Eyes were donated by collaborators who had obtained the animals through the international pet trade (Methods); all animals light adapted and sacrificed in daylight; origin wild or captive-bred not printed. Contrary earlier report printed in the paper: the Introduction says 'P. dolloi appears to possess both single and double cones, while L. paradoxa and N. forsteri possess only single cones (Ali and Anctil, 1973; Bailes et al., 2006).' and the Discussion says 'Pfeiffer (1968) described the retina of P. dolloi in paraffin wax sections, and reported single cones with oil droplets, and double cones with only one member containing an oil droplet.' followed by 'Without a reference image of P. dolloi double cones from Pfeiffer (1968), this is difficult to confirm.'
